clue.text: Non-standard spare parts adapted during print-run

indicators.note: 'Non-' attached to the standard says that piece is taken away from the letters of spare parts
adapted means altered, so the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf or 'up to par'

explanation.surface: Substitute components were modified while the presses were running.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PAR out of SPAREPARTS to leave SEPARTS, which 'adapted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper item that arrives 'at press' turns up while printing is under way.

clue.text: That's the horizon, to the best of my understanding

definitions.meaning: literally, the horizon is the limit of one's sight

definitions.text: to the best of my understanding
definitions.meaning: the idiom meaning in my opinion, from what I know

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally marks the limit of vision and idiomatically the limit of one's knowledge.

clue.text: Water-carrying duo entering arena for Ipswich Town telethon?

indicators.note: entering means going into, so that combination goes inside the football ground

parts.note: Portman Road is Ipswich Town's football ground, abbreviated PORTMAN RD

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the number word surrounds the French water

parts.note: a duo is two
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A pair carrying water into Ipswich Town's stadium for a charity telethon.
explanation.walkthrough: Ipswich Town is an English football club whose home ground is on Portman Road; 'Water' is French here, and the whole clue's last part secretly anagrams to WATER DUO.
explanation.definitionFit: Telethon blends television and marathon, an example of a blended coinage; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Confronted writer cried noisily

indicators.note: noisily signals that the setter's crying phrase is heard, not seen

parts.note: the writer is I, the setter; cried is bawled

explanation.surface: An author faced down shouted and wept.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare them out, facing them down directly.

clue.text: This is sentimental issue for sailors

definitions.meaning: clothes and bedding issued to seamen from the ship's store

explanation.definitionFit: Slop means mawkish sentiment, and naval ready-made kit issued to crews bears the same word.

clue.text: One's after spy leader — Bill Foot, not Smiley

indicators.note: after places the card word behind everything built before it
the leader of the word spy is its opening letter

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement, shortened to ad
F is the standard abbreviation for foot as a unit of length
'One's' reads as 'one is'; one is an ace, the single pip on a card

explanation.surface: Le Carré's world: a spy chief named Bill, someone called Foot, and not George Smiley.
explanation.walkthrough: Smiley looks like le Carré's spy, but here a smiley is the cheerful emoticon; its opposite is the frowning one.
explanation.definitionFit: The frowning emoticon is the contrary of the grinning smiley symbol used in text messages.

clue.text: Not the first put off flight

indicators.note: not the first means the word for put loses its opening letter

parts.note: to put a question is to ask it, so put means asked
addle means gone bad, as an addled egg is off

explanation.surface: Someone not chosen first was put off flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like a phrase, but put is ASKED and off is ADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, the word means a hasty departure, running away in a hurry.

clue.text: To which sank Section G even lower?

parts.note: dept is short for department, a section
the letter that comes one place lower down the alphabet than G

explanation.surface: Section G of an organisation sank to new lows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' means further down the alphabet: the letter after G.
explanation.definitionFit: One sinks to new lows, so this is the level a sinking thing reaches.

clue.text: Stewards' enquiry, is it? That's routine

definitions.meaning: racing stewards hold an enquiry into a race, a question about a horse-racing circuit
the phrase meaning something done naturally, as standard

explanation.definitionFit: Stewards examine a racing incident, literally a thing about the track; idiomatically it means routine practice.

clue.text: Entrances 2,4,6 … admitting degree gowns?

parts.note: 2, 4 and 6 are even numbers

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the degree letter goes inside

parts.note: ingresses are entrances or ways in
D is short for degree, as in a doctorate

explanation.surface: Doorways number 2, 4 and 6 let in graduates in academic gowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gowns' suggests academic robes after 'degree', but it is formal wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal long gowns worn by women at night-time functions.

clue.text: Needing a marker to speak out of turn?

definitions.text: Needing a marker to speak out of turn?

parts.words: Needing a marker to speak out of turn?
parts.note: one who has lost track of their page in a book needs a bookmark; the idiom also means to overstep one's social position and talk out of turn

explanation.surface: Someone needs a cue before they can speak, but blurts out of turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes a reader who has lost their page and needs a bookmark; idiomatically it means behaving above one's station.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose track of your page calls for a bookmark, and the idiom means presuming above your station.

clue.text: Steps taken to make cake half the graduates omitted

indicators.note: omitted means left out, so that piece is removed from the cake

parts.note: a rum baba is a small yeast cake soaked in rum syrup

indicators.note: half of the pair of degree holders means just one of the two

parts.note: two BAs, Bachelors of Arts, are graduates

explanation.surface: Dance steps learned to bake a cake once half the graduates have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the graduates' are BABA (two BAs); 'half' leaves one BA, which 'omitted' removes from RUM BABA.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban ballroom dance is a sequence of steps, so the dance stands for the footwork.

clue.text: What spaces left I filled with dry food

indicators.note: filled with means the abstainer's letters are put into the middle of what comes before
in an across clue, going left means read backwards, right to left

parts.note: 'Eh?' is a way of saying 'what?'
spaces are gaps
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to put in the gaps; their answer is to fill them with dry food.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'left' means read right to left; 'filled with' puts the teetotal letters between the reversed part plus I, giving SPAGHE + TT + I.
explanation.definitionFit: These long dried pasta strands are a staple food, bought dry and boiled.

clue.text: No sleeping partners here?

parts.note: a bed made for one person has room for no companion; a sleeping partner is also a business investor, the misleading sense

explanation.surface: A business with no silent investors, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping partners' are silent investors in business, but here they are literal bedfellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed sized for one person leaves no room for someone to share it.

clue.text: In evil times, old woman's instrument

indicators.note: In placed first says the following pieces go inside the word for evil

parts.note: bad means evil
by is times, as in four by two
gran, grandmother, is an old woman

explanation.surface: In wicked times, an old lady's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small grand piano is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Youngster, crack shot of note

indicators.note: to be shot of something is to be rid of it, so that letter goes

parts.note: Chambers gives spring as a verb meaning to crack or split, as timber does

explanation.surface: A young marksman is a crack shot with a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack shot' looks like a marksman, but crack is SPRING and 'shot of' means rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a slightly dismissive word for a young lad, like a shoot of a family.

clue.text: Shilling rung through again for one enjoying Boxing Day feast

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

indicators.note: through means passing into, so the ladder word goes inside

parts.note: Chambers gives again as a sense of then, as in 'but then'
a rung of a ladder is a step

explanation.surface: A shilling rung up again for someone enjoying a Boxing Day feast.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was an old British coin. 'Boxing Day feast' is 26 December, the saint's feast day from the Good King Wenceslas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Christian martyr's feast day falls on 26 December, Boxing Day in Britain.

clue.text: Having notions one passed on

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
someone who has passed on has died

explanation.surface: Someone full of ideas has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the jokey adjective 'idea'd', meaning furnished with ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed like 'bearded', the adjective means supplied with ideas or thoughts.

clue.text: See 1
Provided for youngster incredibly fast in race

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the word for race

parts.note: a breed is a race or strain of animals

indicators.note: incredibly means beyond belief, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A baby looked after amazingly quickly in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incredibly' makes ASTF; 'fast in race' reads like a quick runner, but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby nursed at the mother's chest has been nourished, so its needs were met that way.

clue.text: See 8
Two will keep on cutting water plant

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the inner group goes into the water word

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water

indicators.note: will keep means holds inside, so the numeral surrounds the cricket word

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Two people will keep cutting a water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the cricket leg side; 'will keep' makes ILEGI, which 'cutting' splits the Latin water around.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbine, the garden flower with spurred petals, is the genus Aquilegia.

clue.text: Superior craft? Superior spinner!

definitions.meaning: a ship plying the Great Lakes, including Lake Superior

explanation.definitionFit: Great Lakes vessels bear this name, as does Jim Laker, the England cricketer famed for spin bowling.

clue.text: Location finder, like the Even Shorter OED?

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: even shorter means the already shortened dictionary word loses another letter, playing on the Shorter OED

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary is a dictionary, shortened to dict

explanation.surface: A finder of places, like the extra-abridged Oxford dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shorter Oxford English Dictionary is a real abridgement; 'Even Shorter' trims DICT to DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Asdic was the early British sonar used to locate submarines underwater.

clue.text: Pronghorn dodging soldier's bolt

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so the insect is left out

parts.note: the pronghorn is a North American antelope-like animal
a soldier ant is a worker type of ant

explanation.surface: A pronghorn escapes a soldier's crossbow bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like a crossbow missile, but it is a verb meaning run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly to marry is to bolt with a lover.

clue.text: Holdings of business family — passing time — runs

parts.note: stock is lineage or family descent
the sands of time run through an hourglass
hares means runs fast

explanation.surface: A family firm's holdings, as time passes, run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Equities and securities held in companies make up a business portfolio.

clue.text: Equipped outside of river bore

indicators.note: outside of means the equipped word sits around the river letter

parts.note: endued means furnished or endowed

explanation.surface: Kitted out for a river bore, the tidal wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tidal wave on a river; it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore as past tense of bear means tolerated or suffered through.

clue.text: Does without iron, ultimately his own

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the cheat word goes around the rest

parts.note: does means cheats or swindles, i.e. cons
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of his

explanation.surface: He manages without his iron, which is ultimately his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; 'own' is the verb meaning admit.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit a fault, so own means acknowledge.
